q: Among the most widely used tools in biology are ____.
e: Among the most widely used tools in biology are microscopes. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: Biologists use these to study cells， cell parts and also organisms that are too small to be seen with naked ____.
e: Biologists use these to study cells, cell parts and also organisms that are too small to be seen with naked eyes. Eyes is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Basically there are two main types of microscope， the light microscope and the ____ microscope.
e: Basically there are two main types of microscope, the light microscope and the electron microscope. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image.

q: The light microscope uses light as a source of radiation to form the image of the specimen being studied while the electron microscope uses ____.
e: The light microscope uses light as a source of radiation to form the image of the specimen being studied while the electron microscope uses electron. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image.

q: Two different types of electron microscopes are commonly used - the transmission electron microscope or TEM and the scanning electron microscope or ____.
e: Two different types of electron microscopes are commonly used - the transmission electron microscope or TEM and the scanning electron microscope or SEM. SEM scans the surface with electrons to give a three-dimensional view. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source.

q: In the TEM， electron is passed through the specimen and allow us to see thin sections of the specimen， and thus the inside ____.
e: In the TEM, electron is passed through the specimen and allow us to see thin sections of the specimen, and thus the inside cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: In SEM the electron beam is passed back and forth over the surface of the specimen. Only the reflected beam is observed and ____ appearance is obtained.
e: In SEM the electron beam is passed back and forth over the surface of the specimen. Only the reflected beam is observed and three dimensional appearance is obtained. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts. Observed size over actual size gives magnification.

q: Usually substage illumination is the light ____.
e: Usually substage illumination is the light source. Source is the biological term this statement needs.

q: By adjusting the iris diaphragm， the amount of light reaching the specimen is ____.
e: By adjusting the iris diaphragm, the amount of light reaching the specimen is controlled. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. The iris diaphragm controls the amount of light reaching the specimen.

q: Condenser focuses the light onto the specimen on the ____.
e: Condenser focuses the light onto the specimen on the slide. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light.

q: Light passing through the specimen is collected by the objective lens and a magnified image is ____.
e: Light passing through the specimen is collected by the objective lens and a magnified image is produced. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power.

q: This lens is responsible for both the magnification and ____.
e: This lens is responsible for both the magnification and resolution. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image formed by the objective ____.
e: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image formed by the objective lens. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power. The eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution.

q: Eyepiece lens focuses the image onto the ____.
e: Eyepiece lens focuses the image onto the eye. The eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution.

q: The electron beam， the specimen and the fluorescent screen must be in the ____.
e: The electron beam, the specimen and the fluorescent screen must be in the vacuum. Electron beams travel in a vacuum, so EM specimens must be specially prepared. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Electron gun and anode emit high velocity electron ____.
e: Electron gun and anode emit high velocity electron beam. SEM scans a beam back and forth over the surface; TEM sends the beam through the specimen. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam onto the ____.
e: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam onto the specimen. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Objective electromagnetic lens focuses and magnified the first ____.
e: Objective electromagnetic lens focuses and magnified the first image. The image is the observed size in the microscope. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power.

q: Projector electromagnetic lenses focus the magnified image onto the ____.
e: Projector electromagnetic lenses focus the magnified image onto the screen. In TEM, projector lenses throw the final image onto a screen.

q: The image of the specimen in black and white is recorded on the screen or photographic ____.
e: The image of the specimen in black and white is recorded on the screen or photographic plate. Plate is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Uses light as a source of radiation. Uses ____ as a source of radiation.
e: Uses light as a source of radiation. Uses electron as a source of radiation. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: The image is projected on the eye or on photographic film. The image is projected on a screen or on photographic ____.
e: The image is projected on the eye or on photographic film. Film is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Preparation of specimen simple， not complicated. Preparation of specimen lengthy and ____.
e: Preparation of specimen simple, not complicated. Preparation of specimen lengthy and complicated.

q: Magnifies up to 2000X Magnifies up to ____ X
e: Magnifies up to 2000X Magnifies up to 500,000 X. 500,000 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Either dead or alive specimen can be examined. Only dehydrated and dead specimen can be ____.
e: Either dead or alive specimen can be examined. Only dehydrated and dead specimen can be examined.

q: Inexpensive to purchase and operate. Expensive to purchase and ____.
e: Inexpensive to purchase and operate. Expensive to purchase and operate.

q: Magnification is the ability to increase the size of the image of the object being studied so that microscopic organisms become ____.
e: Magnification is the ability to increase the size of the image of the object being studied so that microscopic organisms become visible. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Magnification can also be defined as the number of times larger an image is， compared with the real size of the ____.
e: Magnification can also be defined as the number of times larger an image is, compared with the real size of the object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two objects that are close ____.
e: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two objects that are close together. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: If the two objects cannot be resolved they will be seen as a single ____.
e: If the two objects cannot be resolved they will be seen as a single object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Resolving power shows up the smallest detail that a microscope can resolve when imaging an ____.
e: Resolving power shows up the smallest detail that a microscope can resolve when imaging an object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. A microscope magnifies a specimen so hidden cell detail can be seen.

q: An increase in magnification does not always produce a more detail image. It might increases in size but not in ____.
e: An increase in magnification does not always produce a more detail image. It might increases in size but not in detail. Extra magnification without resolution does not add true detail, only a bigger blur. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: But with resolution， the greater the resolution， the greater the ____.
e: But with resolution, the greater the resolution, the greater the detail. Extra magnification without resolution does not add true detail, only a bigger blur. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.
